findings.claim: Repo.Validate's new traversal guard (Name == "." or "..", added in this diff at internal/repos/registry.go) has no corresponding subtest in TestRepoValidate — only the pre-existing reserved-name-fails case ("default"/"archived") is covered.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/repos/registry.go lines 35-61 (git show e5245d08:internal/repos/registry.go): Validate rejects r.Name == "." || r.Name == ".." immediately after the reserved-name check, both new in this diff per `git diff b4981b88...e5245d0 -- internal/repos/registry.go`. Re-read internal/repos/registry_test.go lines 53-62 (git show e5245d08:internal/repos/registry_test.go): TestRepoValidate's only subtest is "reserved-name-fails", looping over ["default","archived"]; no case exercises "." or "..". No other test in the file (TestReload*, TestRegistryAdd, etc.) passes a Name of "." or ".." either. The behavior-changing branch is therefore unexercised by any test — confirms the claim survives re-check.
findings.fix: Add a "traversal-name-fails" case to TestRepoValidate's table (or extend reserved-name-fails) covering Name "." and "..", asserting repo.Validate() errors.

findings.claim: SyncAll's new default-disabled-awaiting-explicit-enable skip branch (routine.DefaultDisabled && overrides[routine.Label] != "enabled") has no darwin test, while the identical behavior change on the Windows side (sched_windows.go's SyncAll) got a dedicated regression test (TestSyncAllSkipsDefaultDisabledNotFoundTask in sched_windows_test.go).
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/routines/bootstrap_darwin.go lines 36-62 (git show e5245d08) and its diff vs b4981b88: the `if routine.DefaultDisabled && overrides[routine.Label] != "enabled"` branch is new in this round. Re-read internal/routines/sched_windows.go lines 140-171 and sched_windows_test.go in full: the Windows SyncAll gained the analogous `state == "NotFound" && routine.DefaultDisabled` skip branch and a matching test that stubs `powershell` and asserts Register-ScheduledTask never fires. `git ls-files internal/routines/` confirms no bootstrap_darwin_test.go exists anywhere in the package — launchctl_darwin_test.go only covers overrideLabels, not SyncAll's loop logic. The asymmetry (tested on one platform, untested on the other, same behavior) is confirmed by direct comparison of both files.
findings.fix: Add a bootstrap_darwin_test.go with a test mirroring TestSyncAllSkipsDefaultDisabledNotFoundTask: stub `launchctl` to report the routine not loaded and no override, mark the routine default-disabled, call SyncAll, and assert Start/`launchctl bootstrap` never fires.

findings.claim: folderDialogScript's addendum-A6 fix (owner.Show()/owner.Activate() before ShowDialog, to bring the Windows folder picker to the foreground) is not pinned by TestFolderDialogScript, which only asserts the pre-existing "ShowDialog($owner)" and "TopMost=$true" substrings — a future edit could silently drop the Show()/Activate() lines without failing any test.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/contextdocs/sync.go lines 88-101 (git show e5245d08) and its diff vs b4981b88: `$owner.Show()` and `$owner.Activate()` are new lines added specifically to fix the addendum A6 regression (dialog opening behind the browser). Re-read internal/contextdocs/sync_test.go (partner, read as context) lines 73-79: TestFolderDialogScript's two assertions ("ShowDialog($owner)", "TopMost=$true") predate this change and do not mention Show() or Activate(). The fix this diff ships is therefore not covered by any assertion.
findings.fix: Add assert.Contains(t, folderDialogScript, "$owner.Show()") and assert.Contains(t, folderDialogScript, "$owner.Activate()") to TestFolderDialogScript.
